Consumer & Culture Trends

Gen Z Mindset

The distinct values, media habits, and expectations of Generation Z consumers that marketers must understand to engage them effectively.

Explanation

Generation Z, generally defined as people born from the late 1990s through the early 2010s, grew up as digital natives with constant access to smartphones and social platforms, which shapes their expectations around authenticity, speed, and two-way brand interaction differently from prior generations. Marketing to this cohort effectively requires more than adjusting media channels; it requires understanding their skepticism toward traditional advertising, preference for creator-driven and peer-validated content, and higher expectations around brand values and transparency. Messaging and formats calibrated for millennial or older audiences frequently fail to land with Gen Z without deliberate adaptation, which is why understanding this mindset matters to marketers.

Related terms

Generation Z, Digital Natives, Creator Economy
